learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Given an array of positive integers and `k`, say whether the array can be split into **k non-empty groups with equal sums**. Every number goes into exactly one group. (n is at most 16.)

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Positive numbers only? (Yes.)
- How large is n? (≤ 16 — exponential search is expected, with pruning.)
- Must every group be non-empty? (Yes; with positive numbers equal sums guarantee it.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: The target per group is fixed: total / k. Place numbers largest first into groups, backtracking. Two prunings make it fast: two groups with the same current sum are interchangeable (try only one), and if a number does not fit into an empty group, no other empty group will help.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "T."he target is total / k; sort descending and place each number into a group that still has room, backtracking — skip groups whose current sum was already tried, and stop after trying one empty group."

learn.title: 5 · Why the approach works

learn.title: 8 · Complexity
learn.md:
**Level 2 — Complexity**

- *Complexity?* — O(k^n) worst case; with pruning far less. The bitmask DP is O(n · 2ⁿ).
- *Bitmask DP?* — dp[mask] = current group's partial sum for the numbers in mask; reachable if some unused number fits.

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Forgetting the quick rejects: total % k ≠ 0, or a number bigger than the target.
- No symmetry pruning — tries the same arrangement k! times.
- Sorting ascending (dead ends are found much later).
